Mr. Smith arrived at the station at 9 a.m. on Monday.
He was carrying a small brown suitcase.
Dr. Brown met him on the platform.
They shook hands and walked to the car.
The drive took about 45 minutes.
Mrs. Brown had prepared lunch for everyone.
After lunch they talked about the project.
The budget was 2.5 million dollars.
Nobody thought it would be enough.
Prof. Green joined them at 3 p.m. that afternoon.

The U.S. government published new figures on Tuesday.
Exports rose by 4.2 percent in the third quarter.
Imports fell slightly, e.g. in cars and machinery.
Analysts had expected a smaller change.
The report runs to 120 pages.
It was written by a team of 15 economists.
Some of them work at universities, i.e. outside the government.
The next report is due in March.
Markets reacted calmly.
Prices on the main index closed 0.3 percent higher.

She lives at 221 Baker St. in London.
Her neighbour is a retired teacher.
They often have tea together in the garden.
The garden has roses, tulips, daisies, etc. and a small pond.
Last year the pond froze over in January.
The children skated on it for a week.
Then the weather turned warm again.
Everyone was surprised by how quickly it melted.
Did you ever see such a winter?
I certainly did not!

Version 3.1.4 of the program fixed several bugs.
The release notes list 27 changes.
One change affects how dates are parsed.
Another one speeds up loading by 30 percent.
Users had asked for that for years.
The developers thanked everyone who reported problems.
The next version will be numbered 3.2.0.
It should appear in about six weeks.
Testing has already begun.
Volunteers are welcome to help.

What time does the museum open?
It opens at 10 a.m. on weekdays.
On weekends it opens an hour later.
Tickets cost 12.50 euros for adults.
Children under 6 enter for free.
The museum has a large collection of old maps.
Some maps are more than 400 years old.
Mr. Lee, the curator, gives a tour every Friday.
The tour lasts about 90 minutes.
Bring comfortable shoes!

Acme Inc. announced record profits yesterday.
The company sells tools, garden furniture, paint, etc. in 30 countries.
Its chief executive, Mrs. Patel, spoke to reporters.
She said the results were better than planned.
The share price rose by 8 percent.
Some investors sold their shares at once.
Others decided to wait.
The annual meeting takes place in May.
Shareholders will vote on a new dividend.
Nobody expects any surprises.

The meeting was moved to 4 p.m. because of the strike.
Trains were cancelled across the whole region.
Many people worked from home instead.
Roads were busier than usual.
The police asked drivers to be patient.
By evening most services were running again.
The union promised further talks next week.
Commuters hope the dispute ends soon.
It has already lasted two months.
Both sides say they want an agreement.

Dr. Adams studied medicine in Boston.
Later she moved to the U.S. west coast.
There she opened a small clinic.
The clinic treats about 50 patients a day.
Most of them come from nearby villages.
Some travel for more than two hours.
Dr. Adams also teaches at the local college.
Her students admire her very much.
She hopes to retire in five years.
Who will take over the clinic then?

The recipe needs 2.5 cups of flour and 3 eggs.
Mix the flour with a pinch of salt.
Add the eggs one at a time.
Stir until the batter is smooth.
Let it rest for 20 minutes.
Heat a pan over medium heat.
Pour in a ladle of batter.
Cook each side for about a minute.
Serve the pancakes warm.
They taste best with fresh fruit, e.g. berries or bananas.

Prof. Martin gave a lecture on ancient Rome.
The hall was full long before 7 p.m.
He spoke for nearly two hours.
Nobody left early.
At the end the audience applauded loudly.
Several students asked questions.
One asked about the fall of the empire.
Prof. Martin smiled and said it was a long story.
He promised to answer it next time.
The next lecture is on Thursday.

St. Mary's church stands in the old town.
It was built in the 12th century.
The tower is 64 metres high.
Visitors can climb it in summer.
From the top you can see the whole valley.
On clear days the mountains are visible.
The church holds concerts every Sunday.
Entry is free, but donations are welcome.
The organ was restored in 1998.
It sounds wonderful.

Mr. and Mrs. Jones celebrated their 50th anniversary.
Their children organised a party.
More than 80 guests came.
There was music, dancing and a large cake.
Mr. Jones gave a short speech.
He thanked his wife for fifty happy years.
Everyone raised a glass.
The party went on until midnight.
It was a night to remember.
The photos are on the family website.

The temperature dropped to minus 12.5 degrees overnight.
Schools stayed closed in several towns.
Buses ran on a reduced timetable.
Doctors warned older people to stay indoors.
The cold spell should end by Saturday.
Forecasters expect rain after that.
Farmers worry about their crops.
Some fields are already damaged.
The government offered help, i.e. low interest loans.
Applications open next month.

Why did the project fail?
There were several reasons.
The plan was unclear from the start.
The team changed three times.
Costs rose from 1.2 to 3.4 million.
Nobody checked the numbers in time.
Mr. Clark, the manager, resigned in June.
His successor tried to save the project.
It was too late.
The lessons are now taught in business schools.

The library opens at 8 a.m. and closes at 8 p.m.
It holds more than 200,000 books.
There is also a large collection of newspapers.
Students use the reading room every day.
The café on the ground floor is popular.
Its coffee costs only 1.80 euros.
Dr. Kim runs the rare books department.
She can show you a printed bible from 1462.
Photography is not allowed there.
Please ask the staff for help.

Wait for me!
I will be there in five minutes.
Please do not leave without me.
The bus leaves at 6.15 tonight.
We cannot miss it.
The next one is not until tomorrow.
Have you packed the tickets?
Yes, they are in my bag.
Good, then we are ready.
Let us go.

Researchers at the U.S. institute tested a new vaccine.
The trial included 3,000 volunteers.
Results were published in a medical journal.
The vaccine was 94.5 percent effective.
Side effects were mild, e.g. a sore arm or a headache.
Regulators will review the data.
A decision is expected within months.
Prof. Ito led the study.
She called the results very encouraging.
Further trials will follow.

The orchestra played Beethoven, Brahms, Mozart, etc. at the festival.
The festival lasts ten days.
Concerts take place in parks and churches.
Most of them are free.
Last year about 40,000 people attended.
The organisers hope for even more this year.
Mrs. Novak conducts the opening concert.
Tickets for it sold out in an hour.
A screen outside will show the concert live.
Bring a blanket and a picnic.

He paid 19.99 dollars for the book.
It was worth every cent.
The story takes place in a small village.
A young girl finds an old key.
Nobody knows what it opens.
She searches the whole village.
In the end she finds a hidden door.
What lies behind it?
You will have to read the book.
I will not tell you!

Dr. Rossi and Prof. Weber wrote the report together.
It covers the years 2010 to 2020.
The main finding is simple.
Cities grew faster than villages.
Young people moved away from the countryside.
Older people stayed behind.
Shops and schools closed in many places.
Some villages are now almost empty.
The authors suggest several measures, e.g. better internet.
The government is studying them.

The train to Paris leaves from platform 4.
It takes about 2.5 hours.
There is a restaurant car on board.
Seats can be reserved online.
First class costs 89 euros.
Second class costs 49 euros.
Children travel at half price.
Dogs are allowed on a lead.
Bicycles must be booked in advance.
Have a pleasant journey!
